subject: AtlasBank spike: model variant + qprofile rollout causing p99 and error-rate surge
messages:
From: Sam Ellison <sam.ellison@atlasbank.com>

Cc: platform-support@atlasbank.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production incident: sudden p99 latency and 502 surge after model switch

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp jump in p99 latency and an increase in 502s around 01:30 UTC this morning, right after the model variant/qprofile switch you performed. Key metrics: p50 unchanged (~80ms), p95 up from 220ms to 480ms, p99 up from 420ms to 1.6s, and 502 rate increased from 0.2% to ~3.4%. Error payloads point to decode stalls and timeouts.

We've attached traces and a brief sample of failing requests. This is impacting our payments flows and triggering SRE alerts. Can you confirm whether a rollback is possible immediately or if you can flip back to the previous qprofile? We need to know ETA for mitigation and whether Redwood can support a hotfix.

Attached: p99_traces_20270322.zip (24MB)

Sam

Subject: Re: Production incident: sudden p99 latency and 502 surge after model switch

Marissa / Jordan — quick technical summary from initial triage:

- Observed correlation between the qprofile change (shifted to v3.2 qprofile with aggressive quantization paths) and a sharp increase in KV cache misses for long prefix requests from Atlas. The miss rate doubled for long sessions, causing more full-decoded steps and kernel fallback that is slower on the current instance type.
- We also see increased batching pressure due to a higher-than-expected token-length distribution in Atlas's workload (more long context requests than the profile used for tuning). That caused queueing and decode stalls at tail percentiles.
- Error 502s correspond to request timeouts in the runtime when decode exceeds the per-token budget.

Mitigation options:
1) Immediate: flip the routing flag to force Atlas traffic to the prior model variant (v3.1 + previous qprofile). This is the fastest rollback path and should restore p99 within 10-20 minutes. Requires coordinated customer notification.
2) Short-term hotfix: enable qprofile compatibility mode to avoid the aggressive quant kernel selection and increase per-request token budget. This would take ~45 minutes to validate and deploy.
3) Medium: tune the qprofile with Atlas-specific token distribution and update kernel selection heuristics; takes 2-3 business days.

Attachments: qprofile_snapshot.yaml (5KB), p99_traces_20270322.zip (24MB)

Recommend option 1 now and option 3 as the follow-up with Atlas on a joint tuning engagement. I'll prepare a rollback playbook and we can run with Jordan to notify Atlas.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: AtlasBank incident update and mitigation plan

Sam — thank you for patience and for the traces. Internal triage complete. Summary and plan:

Summary:
- Root cause: aggressive qprofile/kernels chosen for v3.2 caused KV cache miss amplification and kernel fallback on Atlas's long-session workload, driving p99 latency and request timeouts.
- Impact: p99 and 502 surge for Atlas payments path; customer sees throughput degradation but functional correctness mostly intact.

Actions we will take now:
- Immediate rollback: we are prepared to rollback Atlas traffic to the v3.1 variant and previous qprofile. This will be executed in a controlled window; estimated p99 recovery within 10-25 minutes of cutover.
- Communication: Jordan will notify Atlas and propose a 30-minute maintenance window starting in 60 minutes. If Atlas prefers our compatibility-mode hotfix instead, we can attempt that within 45 minutes, but rollback is fastest.
- Follow-up: Rishi's team will run a postmortem and propose qprofile tuning for Atlas's token distribution and add a canary step to detect KV-miss amplifications in future rollouts.

Please confirm whether you want us to proceed with the rollback in 60 minutes. We will pause if you prefer the hotfix path.

Attachments: rollout_playbook.md (stub), contact_list_execs.txt (stub)

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
